walkthroughs.body_html:
Always check units first.

Convert cm to m, g to kg, etc.

For V = IR: triangle with V on top, I and R below.

Cover what you want.

Match sig figs to the least precise data.

Usually 2-3 sf at GCSE.

mcqs.q: If an object is moving at constant velocity in a straight line, what is the net force on it?
options: Heat is measured in degrees Celsius and temperature in Joules.
There must be a forward force on the object to keep it moving.
The net force equals the velocity times the mass of the object.
Zero — by Newton's first law, constant velocity requires zero net force.

mcqs.q: When you push a wall, what does Newton's third law say about the wall?
options: The wall only pushes back if your force is strong enough to make it react.
The wall pushes back with a force proportional to how stiff it is, not equal to your force.
The wall exerts an equal and opposite force on you at the same instant.
Heat is measured in degrees Celsius and temperature in Joules.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between heat and temperature?
options: The wall pushes back with a force proportional to how stiff it is, not equal to your force.
Heat is the energy transferred due to temperature difference; temperature measures average kinetic energy of particles.
Heat and temperature are the same thing — both measure how hot something is.
Heat is measured in degrees Celsius and temperature in Joules.
